0.6.0 shows the content that a page keeps in shadow DOM, which pages saved with their web components
can contain, as the rest of the page, with its images, stylesheets, and tooltips. Links to vault
files open from the page's own tab, a tab moved to another tab group or window keeps its page's
place and style, and the viewer reads a page's stylesheets more as browsers do. This personal fork
supports Linux desktop. macOS and mobile are out of scope, and this release is marked desktop-only.
Windows supplies additional development checks. The fork is not in Obsidian's community plugin
directory; install it by hand.

## Install

1. Download `viell-html-page-viewer-0.6.0.zip` below.
2. Unzip it into your vault's `.obsidian/plugins/` folder, so that
   `.obsidian/plugins/viell-html-page-viewer/` holds `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css`,
   replacing those of an earlier version.
3. In Obsidian, open **Settings → Community plugins**. If upstream's **HTML Page Viewer** is
   installed, turn it off: both plugins open `.html` and `.htm` files. Then turn on **HTML Page
   Viewer (viell)**, or turn it off and on again if it was on; if it is not listed yet, reload the
   list of installed plugins.

To go back, install 0.5.2 the same way. Settings are kept. The plugin never changes your notes or
pages.

## What is new

- **Shadow DOM is shown as the rest of the page.** Its images load, also those that it names by
  file name only, and its stylesheets and their imports apply. With **Local files with scripts
  on**, its files are copied into a page with scripts on too. Find searches and highlights its text,
  its links and images show tooltips, and the split view's two sides stay in step on such a page.
- **Tooltips on SVG links.** Hovering an SVG link that nothing inside names shows where it leads.
  An SVG link with text, a labelled or titled shape, a `<use>` icon, or HTML content inside keeps
  the name that its content gives it, for screen readers, and shows no tooltip.

## Changed

- **A link to a vault file opens from the page's own tab**, as a link in a note in that tab does: in
  that tab, or with Ctrl-click or a middle click in a new tab beside it. Before, it opened from
  whichever tab was active, which was not always the page's: a click inside a page never makes its
  tab the active one. A link in a pinned tab opens where one in a pinned note does. **In a
  sidebar**, a plain click now opens the link in the sidebar's tab, in place of the page, as one in
  a note there does; Ctrl-click or a middle click opens a new tab in the main area, as before.

## Fixed

- When its tab moves to another tab group or window, a page keeps the theme and line width that it
  shows and, if it scrolls as a whole, its place, and the split view's two sides stay in step there.
  On Obsidian 1.5.3, the **Source** view stays scrolled as far as it was, instead of starting again
  from its top.
- A page follows a change of Obsidian's theme or of **Readable line length** made while the viewer
  was still preparing it.
- A tab no longer shows a page's earlier contents under another page's name when the first page
  changes on disk just as the other opens in the tab. Nothing was written to either file.
- Find in the page leaves out fallback content and SVG resources that Obsidian never paints, and
  finds a closed select's chosen option. Opening the find bar without a query no longer collects
  the page's text.
- The viewer reads a page's stylesheets more as browsers do:
  - text inside CSS strings and comments, such as `content: "url(icon.png)"`, stays as the page has
    it, and repeated malformed `url(` text no longer stalls preparing the page;
  - only the imports that browsers apply are read into the page: those at a stylesheet's start, not
    one after a style rule or inside a block;
  - an imported stylesheet that ends inside a string, a comment, an unquoted `url(`, or a block no
    longer drops the rules after its import;
  - an import into a cascade layer stays an import also when a comment or an escape comes before
    `layer`;
  - only the text of HTML and SVG `<style>` elements, not of their child elements, and HTML
    stylesheet links are read as stylesheets: text inside an SVG `<style>`'s child elements and a
    `<link>` inside SVG or MathML no longer apply, a MathML `<style>` no longer reads or copies
    anything, and a page whose only styles are such elements now shows in Obsidian's theme;
  - unquoted URLs with an escaped `)` or `"` resolve, and a linked stylesheet that imports itself no
    longer repeats its rules.

  Before 0.6.0, the viewer also read the stylesheets, and with **Local files with scripts on**
  copied the files, that only such text or ignored rules named. Each read and copy still kept to the
  vault, to `.css` files for stylesheets, and to the setting's file types and size limits, so a page
  gained no file that it could not name in CSS that applies. The
  [security model](https://github.com/viell-dev/slop-html-page-viewer/blob/0.6.0/SECURITY.md#security-model)
  describes what the viewer reads.

## Known limits

- With scripts on, the find bar searches only the source, split-view scrolling is independent, links
  work as in a browser frame, and a page starts again from its top, running its scripts again, when
  its tab moves to another tab group or window. Local files load only with **Local files with
  scripts on**, within its 8 MB per-file and 32 MB per-page limits. Files loaded by scripts
  themselves, imported modules, and pages in frames do not load.
- Stylesheets from the web do not apply, apart from Google Fonts. Local stylesheets must end in
  `.css`. Imports of vault stylesheets into cascade layers or with support conditions do not apply
  ([#151](https://github.com/viell-dev/slop-html-page-viewer/issues/151)), and an import that stays
  an import after an inlined one, such as a Google Fonts import after a local one, can be ignored
  ([#152](https://github.com/viell-dev/slop-html-page-viewer/issues/152)). A `<style>` or `<link>`
  applies whatever its `type` or `disabled` attribute says
  ([#147](https://github.com/viell-dev/slop-html-page-viewer/issues/147)).
- A page whose stylesheets import each other many times can keep the viewer preparing it for a long
  time ([#154](https://github.com/viell-dev/slop-html-page-viewer/issues/154)).
- After a tab moves, parts of a page that scroll by themselves start again from their beginning, and
  parts that the page opened, such as a `<details>` element, are closed again.
- A link to a part of another page opens that page at its top. A link that SVG `<use>` copies from
  elsewhere in the page does nothing when clicked.
- Find does not highlight a closed select's chosen option, and does not search multiple selects,
  list boxes, or option labels. A match stays within one shadow root.

## Testing

Tested in Linux Obsidian 1.5.3 and 1.15.1: page rendering with shadow DOM, its stylesheets and
imports, and copying files with scripts on; the page's protections; links, also from tabs that are
not the active one, in other tab groups and windows; tooltips; find; split view; moving tabs to
other tab groups and windows; refreshing and leaving a tab without writing any file; installing this
release's zip, turning the plugin off and on, updating it, and restarting Obsidian; and the
synthetic archive corpus compared with the frozen prototype. Links in a page in a sidebar were
checked in both versions while the change was reviewed, not in the automated tests. Build and unit
checks also run on Windows. `SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of the files below.
